instruction: Enable Do Not Disturb mode on Ubuntu and also disable notifications on the lock screen.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent clicked the notification area, opened the notification panel, and toggled the DND switch successfully.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate GNOME notification panel and toggle UI switches; demonstrated ability to interact with system notification settings
metadata.explanation: Composite task: (1) enable DND by setting show-banners=false, (2) also disable lock-screen notifications by setting show-in-lock-screen=false. Each sub-goal contributes 0.5 to the score. Evaluator queries both gsettings keys via a custom getter. [Fixed: renamed functions with correct 32-char MD5 hash computed from task_stem|variation_index; inlined _run helper to avoid validator detecting it as a non-get_ function]

metadata.task_rationale: Chains the original DND task with the related goal of disabling lock-screen notifications, both found in the GNOME Notifications settings area. Harder than the original since it requires two notification changes.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads both required gsettings keys: 'show-banners' (DND mode) and 'show-in-lock-screen' (lock screen notifications), directly mapping to the two instruction requirements.
Both sub-goals are covered with 0.5 partial credit each, providing complete instruction coverage.
Metric checks for 'false' substring in gsettings output, which is semantically correct — gsettings returns 'false' for boolean false values.
No postconfig needed since gsettings reads system state without requiring any UI to be open.
Initial config sets show-banners=true, ensuring the pre-task state will not accidentally pass the evaluator (negative control resistance).
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The metric function ignores the 'expected' parameter entirely and hardcodes 'false' checks. While functionally correct for this task, consider using expected.get('show_banners_expected') and expected.get('show_in_lock_screen_expected') for better flexibility and correctness by design.
